thread.title: Sen. Rick Scott and Rep. Andy Ogles urge action on cybersecurity threats from China
thread.title_full: Sen. Rick Scott and Rep. Andy Ogles urge action on cybersecurity threats from China

author: Sunshine Sentinel
title: Sen. Rick Scott and Rep. Andy Ogles urge action on cybersecurity threats from China
text:
Senator Rick Scott and Representative Andy Ogles called for urgent action to strengthen U.S. cybersecurity against potential attacks from China, according to a May 20 statement. They are advocating for the passage of the Strengthening Cyber Resilience Against State-Sponsored Threats Act, which aims to address vulnerabilities in American infrastructure.
The lawmakers said that America’s reliance on digital technology has brought significant benefits but also created new risks. “Now, imagine if tomorrow that access we’ve become familiar and comfortable with became our biggest threat,” Scott and Ogles said in their joint statement. They warned that groups backed by the Chinese Communist Party (CCP), such as “Volt Typhoon” and “Salt Typhoon,” have targeted key sectors including energy, water systems, transportation, and communications.
Scott and Ogles highlighted specific dangers: “If a hospital is locked out of its systems, life support could fail and patients would die.” They added that an attack on the electrical grid could leave millions without heat or power, while financial system breaches could wipe out bank accounts or erase records of stock ownership.
To address these threats, they are pushing for legislation that would create a joint task force led by the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) to detect and respond to CCP-backed cyber threats. The bill also requires CISA to provide annual reports to Congress with threat assessments and recommendations. According to Scott’s official website , he serves on several Senate committees related to national security issues.
Scott emphasized the nonpartisan nature of this issue: “This is not a partisan game; it is literally a matter of the lights turning on when you hit the switch.” He said leaving agencies like CISA unfunded increases vulnerability for American families.
In conclusion, Scott stated: “Our bill makes Americans safer, it protects our way of life, and it strengthens our national security.” He urged quick passage in the Senate so President Trump can sign it into law.
